source_title: US Election Day forecast: Storm threatens to dampen voter turnout in key states
source_excerpt: Rain could affect voter turnout in parts of the central United States on midterm election day, as a storm threatens to bring wet and windy weather to several states with key races. More than 35 million people have already voted early, but those heading to polling stations on Tuesday may face rain depending on the stormâs path.Multiple studies cited by CNN have found that rain and bad weather tend to keep voters away from polling stations, while sunshine has the opposite effect. The extent of the impact will depend on which areas receive rainfall.The storm could bring rain from parts of the Great Lakes and Upper Midwest to the western Gulf Coast. However, its exact path remains uncertain, with some areas potentially staying dry while others could experience steady rain or passing showers. However, coastal areas of the Mid-Atlantic and Southeast could see light showers.Most of the eastern half of the country is forecast to experience temperatures 5 to 15 degrees Fahrenheit above average.
